stages.failureClassification: site-specific-difference (true-positive detection; underlying cause is the known-limitation that brand assets are never auto-fetched)
stages.detail: 'served head contains no source-brand term' fails on every route because React 19 auto-hoists <link rel=preload as=image> for eager images into the head, and those URLs live on https://nextjs.org/_next/static/... — on a site whose brand IS its hostname, every un-internalized asset URL is a brand leak. The check is a true positive (head really carries source-brand strings); stripe passed only because its asset hosts differ from its brand terms' casing/host. Composition note: seo:qa runs without the asset-rewrite layer chained, and even the full chain would not fix it here since the leaking assets are replacement-required (never fetched by policy).

stages.failureClassification: known-limitation (policy) + generic-engine-defect (one fetch candidate) + live-source-instability none
stages.detail: nextjs.org's asset population is dominated by brand marks (vercel/nextjs logotypes, partner logos, avatars) — the conservative classifier correctly refuses 154 of 214, so asset independence is near-zero without operator replacements. That is the policy working, not failing. Fetch failures: (a) ai000001 https://nextjs.org/%23b http-error — a CSS url(#b) SVG fragment reference mis-inventoried as a fetchable page URL (generic engine defect, see below); (b) blog mp4 rejected too-large — the size bound working as designed.

stages.detail: the 2 FAILs are interactions-desktop:/ and interactions-mobile:/ 'clicked=1 regionsAppeared=0'. The homepage's clickable P1 trigger on nextjs.org is a SELECTION pattern (aria-checked toggle) that legitimately mounts no region — parity/theme QA proved the state flip works ('state aria-checked=true, regions 0', equivalent 2/2). production:qa's absolute regionsAppeared>0 assertion encodes stripe's disclosure/menu trigger shape and false-fails selection-type triggers. Theme lineage used the QA-passed original theme run (both curated themes honestly failed browser QA and were not forced in).
